# monaparte

> A conversational assistant whose language model runs entirely in the
> visitor's browser. No inference server, no account, no data leaving the
> device. It is the reference demo for aparté, a chat-interface library.

Written in French and English (the interface follows the browser locale). The
site is a single page: `/chat/<id>` addresses a conversation that exists only
in the visitor's own browser storage, so those URLs carry no content and are
not worth citing — link to the root instead.

## What actually runs

The model is downloaded from Hugging Face on first visit (~1.1 GB, cached by
the browser afterwards) and executed locally through transformers.js on WebGPU,
falling back to WebAssembly. Nothing is sent to a server at any point — there
is no inference backend to send it to. The page is static files behind nginx.

One shared base model serves every capability. Specialised behaviours are LoRA
adapters swapped in at call time ("souffleurs" — prompters), and image
understanding is a separate vision encoder attached the same way, on demand.
That is why the whole thing fits in one download rather than several models.

- [Model weights and adapters](https://huggingface.co/maxituc/aparte-souffleurs): the base model, the LoRA adapters, and the vision encoder.

## Tools the assistant can use

Reading an attached file (including describing an image), producing xlsx/docx/pdf
documents, deterministic file conversion, exact computation in a sandbox,
charts and code artefacts, local reminders, and asking the user a clarifying
question. All of it executes in the browser.

## Requirements and limits

- WebAssembly is required; WebGPU makes it usable rather than merely possible.
- A secure context (HTTPS) and cross-origin isolation are required — the page
  sends `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`, without
  which `SharedArrayBuffer` is unavailable and inference crawls.
- The first visit downloads about 1.1 GB. Later visits load from cache.
- The model is small. It is meant to show what an on-device assistant can do,
  not to compete with a hosted frontier model.

## Related

- [aparté](https://apartejs.dev): the chat-interface library this site demonstrates.
- [aparté changelog](https://apartejs.dev/changelog/): what changed, per release.
